details: io-uring 0.7 and libc 0.2 remain target_os=linux dependencies.
The inherited engine real module remains cfg(target_os=linux).
Inherited engine storage and prefetch call sites continue to construct stream::fetch::Fetcher with the existing split-shard API.
The new PositionalSource is additive; no inherited Linux engine call site selects it by default.
The kernel build continues to return immediately unless CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS is linux.
PULSAR_CUDA_ARCH remains an explicit override; the inherited default request remains 61,75,80,86,89 filtered against nvcc support when available.
PULSAR_GPU remains the explicit device override; otherwise inherited primary-device selection remains measured H2D bandwidth with the existing tie-breaks and CUDA device-zero fallback.
The engine continues to use the inherited CUDA-backed implementation only inside its Linux-gated real module.

short_payload_boundary.ignore_reason: inherited fetch_each currently accepts short CQE; requires separately evidenced Linux hardening
short_payload_boundary.observed_implementation_debt: The inherited fetch_each completion path does not currently compare the CQE byte count with payload_offset + payload_len before reporting success.
short_payload_boundary.claim: Short-payload failure semantics are not verified and are not fixed by this feature. The ignored test must remain visible until a separately reviewed Linux hardening change is executed on suitable hardware.

warnings: Exit code 0 from either cargo test command is not a Linux/CUDA pass because every relevant test was cfg-excluded and the observed count was zero.

The Linux preservation test helpers may report an in-test SKIP when io_uring or O_DIRECT is unavailable even on Linux; future evidence must record such skips rather than counting them as executed semantic coverage.
Static source identity and additive-surface review cannot establish compiler, runtime, I/O, numerical, or performance parity on Linux/CUDA.
The ignored short-payload test records inherited unresolved behavior and prevents a claim that all named Linux storage semantics have passed.
blockers: A supported Linux host with io_uring and O_DIRECT is required to execute the named stream preservation suite.
A supported NVIDIA GPU, CUDA toolkit, and Linux host or suitable CI are required to compile and execute inherited CUDA selftests.
The inherited short-CQE behavior requires separately reviewed Linux hardening before the ignored short-payload assertion can be enabled and evidenced.

claim_policy.prohibited_claim: The shared storage or routing changes are Linux/CUDA-safe.
claim_policy.required_claim: Inherited Linux/CUDA selection and defaults are unchanged by static review, but Linux, io_uring, O_DIRECT, and CUDA runtime compatibility remain unavailable and unverified at tested commit 8abdfe0.
